unit.title: Si Clauses: The Impossible Past
unit.subtitle: The third conditional — undoing what already happened

grammar.title: Rewriting a past that can never change
grammar.intro: The third conditional talks about an unreal past: things that didn't happen, and the results they would have had. The recipe is fixed: si + pluperfect subjunctive (hubiera + participle) in the condition, and the conditional perfect (habría + participle) in the result. One iron rule sits underneath it all: the si half never takes a conditional.

sections.heading: si + hubiera + ..., + habría + ...
sections.body: The si clause uses the pluperfect subjunctive; the main clause uses the conditional perfect (habría, habrías, habría, habríamos, habríais, habrían + participle):

ex.en: If I had known, I would have come.

ex.es: Si me lo hubieras dicho, te habría ayudado.
ex.en: If you had told me, I would have helped you.

sections.heading: Two common variations
sections.body: First, the -ra form can replace habría in the result (…, hubiera venido). Second, mixed conditionals link a past condition to a present result — the main clause becomes the simple conditional:

ex.en: If I had known, I would have come.

ex.es: Si hubiera estudiado, ahora tendría un buen trabajo.
ex.en: If I had studied, I would now have a good job.

sections.heading: The iron rule + a shortcut
sections.body: Never put a conditional in the si clause: it's si hubiera, never si habría (and certainly not 'si hubría'). A neat shortcut for the condition is de + haber + participle, which replaces the whole 'si' clause:

ex.en: Had I known it, I would have come.
If I had been able to, I would have called you.

takeaways: Third conditional: si + pluperfect subjunctive, then conditional perfect (habría + participle).
The -ra form can replace habría: …, hubiera venido.
Never 'si habría' — the si clause always takes hubiera. Shortcut: De haberlo sabido…

mistakes.why: The si clause never takes a conditional. Use the pluperfect subjunctive: si hubiera sabido.

mistakes.w: Si me lo hubieras dicho, te ayudaba.
mistakes.r: Si me lo hubieras dicho, te habría ayudado.
mistakes.why: An unreal past result needs the conditional perfect (habría ayudado), not the imperfect.

mistakes.w: Si hubiera estudiado, ahora tendría... si hubría estudiado.
mistakes.r: Si hubiera estudiado, ahora tendría un buen trabajo.
mistakes.why: There is no form 'hubría'. The condition is hubiera; a present result takes the simple conditional (tendría).

exercises.prompt_en: If I had known, I would have come.
exercises.no: The si clause never takes a conditional — use “hubiera sabido”.

exercises.prompt: Si me lo hubieras dicho, te ___. (ayudar, yo)
exercises.prompt_en: If you had told me, I would have helped you.
exercises.ok: ¡Exacto! El resultado → condicional compuesto: habría ayudado.
exercises.no: The result of an unreal past takes the conditional perfect: “te habría ayudado”.

exercises.prompt: Build: “If I had studied, I would now have a good job.”
exercises.no: “Si hubiera estudiado, ahora tendría un buen trabajo” — past cause, present result.

exercises.prompt_en: If I had been able to, I would have called you.
exercises.hint: Conditional perfect (habría + participle) — or the -ra variant.
exercises.no: The result is “habría llamado” (the -ra form “hubiera llamado” also works).

exercises.prompt: Match each condition to its natural result.

exercises.tts: Si me lo hubieras dicho, te habría ayudado.
accepted: si me lo hubieras dicho te habria ayudado
exercises.translation: If you had told me, I would have helped you.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! “Si me lo hubieras dicho, te habría ayudado.”
exercises.no: It was: “Si me lo hubieras dicho, te habría ayudado.” (If you had told me, I would have helped you.)

exercises.scenario: A colleague explains why he missed a deadline 🕒

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.es: No sabía que la entrega era ayer. Nadie me avisó.
lines.en: I didn't know the deadline was yesterday. Nobody told me.

options.text: Si me lo hubieras preguntado, te lo habría dicho.
Si me lo habrías preguntado, te lo habría dicho.
Si me lo preguntabas, te lo diría.

exercises.no: The si clause takes hubieras, the result takes habría: “Si me lo hubieras preguntado, te lo habría dicho”.

exercises.en: Had I known it, I would have come.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the sound of “De haberlo sabido, habría venido.”
